Homage to her whose face is like A hundred full autumn moons gathered together, Blazing with the brilliant light Of a thousand gathered stars.
Homage to you, whose two eyes are as brilliant As the light of the full sun and moon; By reciting HARA twice and TUTTĀRE, You dispel the most violent contagious diseases.
Homage to the Uṣṇīṣa of the Tathāgatas, She who acts with infinite, complete victory, She who is deeply relied upon by the Victors' heirs, Having attained every single perfection without exception.

Oceans of Buddhas, both those who have come and those yet to come, Hold the holy Dharma as their life-force in all infinite realms; O Jetsunma, please grant that my aspirations be fulfilled, Which teach the supreme conduct of awakening to perfection.

You have perfectly accomplished generosity and ethical discipline, And practiced patience and diligence; Having reached the culmination of meditative concentration and wisdom, I prostrate to you, who have perfected the perfections.

Proclaiming the Dharma with the profound melody of Brahmā, And teaching the vast, uninterrupted continuity, Sever all the webs of the three obscurations, And grant the relief of the throne of enlightenment, O Jetsunma.

Even if the bardo appears for but a fleeting moment, May the emanation and reabsorption of the pure mandala be complete; In the Lotus Array of Great Bliss and other such realms, O Jetsunma, please lead me to a pure land.

Your body is the full autumn moon in the center of a lotus, The youthful bloom of vajra-bliss perfectly complete; With an infinite mandala of stainless light, Bestow the enlightened activities of the four rites, O Jetsunma.
Homage to you, blissful, virtuous, and peaceful, Whose very sphere of experience is the peace of nirvāṇa; Perfectly endowed with SVĀHĀ and OṀ, You are the one who destroys great negativity.

May the supreme teachings of the Victor, the source of benefit and happiness, Flourish and spread throughout the ten directions without ever declining, And may the lives of all those sublime great beings who uphold them Be extended for a long time, O Jetsunma.

Beneath the sovereign Bodhi tree, you pervaded the earth and sky, subduing the hosts of Māra, Who rained down a shower of vajras, short spears, wheels, fire, mountains, and ranges of snow-peaks. When the powerful one, adorned with flower-arrows, strove to obstruct your enlightenment through miraculous displays, You defeated them well with a heart of loving-kindness; I bow my head to you, the one who attained perfect Buddhahood.

Constant in continuity and all-pervading like space, Through spontaneously accomplished enlightened activity, You fulfill the hopes of those to be trained, O Lord of the Wish-Fulfilling Tree; I prostrate to the Noble Lady, the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel.

The five Sakya patriarchs, Marpa, Milarepa, and Gampopa, Mañjughoṣa Lama and all the other Indian and Tibetan Assemblies of learned and accomplished vidyādharas, The peaceful and wrathful yidams, ḍākinīs, dharma protectors, and so forth— I invoke you from the depths of your heart; look upon us with your compassion!

Since you are lords of the ten strengths and possess the ten masteries, Restore these declining teachings to their original state, And may those who are authoritative, learned, disciplined, and accomplished, Manifest in many forms to restore the teachings.

Mother of all the Victors, medicine that dispels torment, Loving nurse, the sole kinsman of all living beings; Throughout the garland of my lives, I have no other, So I take refuge in you until I reach the heart of enlightenment.

In brief, to you, the Noble Lady, who is the single embodiment Of the primordial wisdom of all the Victors and their heirs, I pray with heartfelt devotion: Hold me in your care until I reach enlightenment.
In both India and Tibet, may the precious lamp Of the festival of a later golden age be lit, And may the lotus grove of the Buddha's non-sectarian teachings reach its full bloom.
Thus, the Guru of beings, of the Śākya lineage, Born from the royal line of the Ikṣvāku, By this praise of the Bhagavan, the Perfect Buddha, May beings swiftly attain omniscience.
In short, since you are the essence of refuge, Until I attain enlightenment, always Do not let me fall under the power of obstructing demons, But grant your grace to perfect the twofold benefit.

Possessing the eye of wisdom, free from the dust of profound insight, And the excellent conduct of one whose afflictions gradually diminish, With great respect for the training, and with mindfulness and vigilance, O Jetsunma, please blend my mind-stream with the Dharma.

By the power of the two accumulations gathered since beginningless time, You have attained an inconceivable body of space; Because I pray with one-pointed longing, Do not diminish your compassionate blessings, O Jetsunma.

Those who bear the victory banner of saffron robes and the discipline of renunciation, Bodhisattvas who possess genuine, unfeigned altruism, And mantra-holders of the generation and completion stages who maintain their samaya— To those who have become like a painted lamp, You who possess the eye of primordial wisdom, Please look upon us with certainty and protect us with your compassion!

May the lives of the masters who uphold the teachings be firm, And may the lifespan and merit of the patrons of the teachings increase. May those who harm the teachings be reduced to nothing but their names, And may the victory banner of the teachings be raised in the ten directions!
Homage to you, majestic in your supreme joy, Who spread garlands of light as your crown ornament, Who, with the laughter of TUTTĀRE, Bring demons and the world under your power.

O Deity in whom I have placed my trust for this life and the next, O Bhagavatī, who has become the Mother of the Victors of the three times, If you do not bring the fruits of my prayers to fruition, I have no other refuge, O Jetsunma.

Upon the tip of the precious stem between the thumb and ring finger, From a lovely lotus that has newly blossomed, You pour forth nectar of every supreme and common kind; Bring delight to my mind, O Jetsunma.

Conceptual thoughts following habitual tendencies are like ripples on water; In each and every instant, I accumulate many causes for the miserable realms. Of this never-ending seed of cyclic existence, Please cut the root right now, O Jetsunma.
When the protector of beings was first born, All the wise ones of the world rejoiced; The hosts of Māra were filled with great anxiety, And all the non-Buddhist extremists were terrified.
Your scriptural speech is a lion’s roar; When proclaimed to the world including the gods, Brahmā and Viṣṇu were rendered speechless, And the teachers of the gods shrank away like foxes.

With your palm that grants the supreme gift of fulfilling all wishes— Through which touching brings Dharma, wealth, desire, and liberation, And which is formed from a hundred merits— Anoint the crown of my head, O Jetsunma.

Because you have attained in every way The phenomena as they are and as they exist, I prostrate to you, who have accomplished The enlightened activities as you intended.

In particular, the profound meaning of the essential definitive truth, May those with the good fortune to hear it have it settle in their ears; May the hosts of gods, nāgas, and yakṣas who delight in this, Raise its status to the very heights of heaven, O Jetsunma.
Thus, the Guru of beings, of the Śākya lineage, Born from the royal line of the Ikṣvāku, By this praise of the Bhagavan, the Perfect Buddha, May beings swiftly attain omniscience.

Even when I see that the fruits of karma are ripening before my eyes, I still have not developed faith in karma and its results; Like a beast of prey in saffron robes, Please lead my mind toward virtue, O Jetsunma.

You have perfectly accomplished generosity and ethical discipline, And practiced patience and diligence; Having reached the culmination of meditative concentration and wisdom, I prostrate to you, who have perfected the perfections.

The Buddha's teachings of the Vinaya, Sūtra, and Abhidharma, Along with the four great classes of the Secret Mantra Tantras, The ten great pillars of the scriptural lineages in the Land of Snows, And the eight great chariots of the practice lineages, and so forth— Behold how all the systems of the Buddha’s teachings, both Sūtra and Mantra, Have now fallen into a state of extreme decline!

All the misdeeds, obscurations, faults, and downfalls accumulated since beginningless time, May they be purified and cleansed within this physical support; And until that time, grant me the glory of harmony with the Dharma, And the siddhi of deathless life-empowerment, O Jetsunma.

Through this suffering that I am currently experiencing, May the causes and effects of the suffering of all beings Be swiftly exhausted, and from now on, may I lead all beings, myself and others, From happiness to ever-greater happiness, O Jetsunma.

May the lives of the masters who uphold the teachings be firm, And may the lifespan and merit of the patrons of the teachings increase. May those who harm the teachings be reduced to nothing but their names, And may the victory banner of the teachings be raised in the ten directions!
In both India and Tibet, may the precious lamp Of the festival of a later golden age be lit, And may the lotus grove of the Buddha's non-sectarian teachings reach its full bloom.

With Ture, the very moment one remembers your feet, Through your display of names and forms to tame beings according to their needs, You protect from all the misfortunes of the view of self; I prostrate to the Mother, the Swift and Compassionate One.
Furthermore, may the flowers of the fourfold perfections bloom in beauty for the time being, And ultimately, I pray that you grant the ripening fruit Of the union of the indivisible three kāyas.
The profound and supremely peaceful expanse, Completely free from directions and partiality— In the moment of your blessing, Please cause subject and object to dissolve into the central channel.
Homage to you, who strike the surface of the earth With your palms and trample it with your feet; With a wrathful frown and the syllable HŪṀ, You shatter the seven levels.

Conceptual thoughts following habitual tendencies are like ripples on water; In each and every instant, I accumulate many causes for the miserable realms. Of this never-ending seed of cyclic existence, Please cut the root right now, O Jetsunma.
The second Buddha, Padmākara, Lord of a hundred thousand ḍākinīs, holder of the secret mantra treasury, Bodhisattva Prince Rolpa Tsal, I pray to you: grant the supreme and ordinary accomplishments!

Even when I see that the fruits of karma are ripening before my eyes, I still have not developed faith in karma and its results; Like a beast of prey in saffron robes, Please lead my mind toward virtue, O Jetsunma.
Your scriptural speech is a lion’s roar; When proclaimed to the world including the gods, Brahmā and Viṣṇu were rendered speechless, And the teachers of the gods shrank away like foxes.
The profound and supremely peaceful expanse, Completely free from directions and partiality— In the moment of your blessing, Please cause subject and object to dissolve into the central channel.

More distinguished than the thousand buddhas of this fortunate aeon, Noble and wondrous as the uḍumbara flower, You who took hold of this realm during this age of strife, Homage to the Supreme Sage, the Fulfiller of All Aims.

Conceptual thoughts following habitual tendencies are like ripples on water; In each and every instant, I accumulate many causes for the miserable realms. Of this never-ending seed of cyclic existence, Please cut the root right now, O Jetsunma.

O Deity in whom I have placed my trust for this life and the next, O Bhagavatī, who has become the Mother of the Victors of the three times, If you do not bring the fruits of my prayers to fruition, I have no other refuge, O Jetsunma.

With the precious vessel of your bodhicitta, O Tāre, From the ocean of suffering in cyclic existence and the lower realms, You constantly liberate all sentient beings, as vast as space; I prostrate to the Noble Mother, Jetsunma Drolma.

Upon the tip of the precious stem between the thumb and ring finger, From a lovely lotus that has newly blossomed, You pour forth nectar of every supreme and common kind; Bring delight to my mind, O Jetsunma.
With the crowns of gods and demigods, Bowing down before your lotus feet, To you who liberate from all misfortune, Mother Tārā, I offer this homage.
Your son is Mañjughoṣa, Your disciple is Śāradvatīputra, You have made Maitreya your supreme regent; Who could possibly doubt this?

May the lives of the masters who uphold the teachings be firm, And may the lifespan and merit of the patrons of the teachings increase. May those who harm the teachings be reduced to nothing but their names, And may the victory banner of the teachings be raised in the ten directions!
